newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Guidant to seek stent approval.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Guidant to seek stent approval.

text.p: Guidant Corp will apply to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration this quarter for marketing approval for its Multi-Link stent, said chief executive Ronald Dollens on Monday.

In an interview with Reuters, Dollens said sales of the stent have been strong in Europe, but it remains unavailable in the United States -- a key obstacle to turning around the performance of the company's vascular intervention business.
Sales in the division were $100.8 million in the first quarter, down from $106.9 million in the year-ago period.
"If you net out the (exchange) rate impacts and the atherectomy trends...what one sees is a flat year-over-year" sales picture for the division, Dollens said.
"Until we get the Multi-Link stent available in the U.S., that's generally what it's going to look like," he said, adding: "We will do the submission this quarter to the FDA."
Shares in Indiana-based Guidant closed off 3/8 to 59-1/2.

In its other primary business line, Guidant reported Monday that cardiac rhythm management sales were up 11 percent versus the year-ago level, a lower growth rate compared with the fourth quarter's 23 percent.
"The difference ends up being the (exchange) rate impact outside the United States plus some pricing pressure...outside the U.S.," Dollens said.
For sales overall, he said: "We are still comfortable with high single digit" growth rates.
The company reported total first quarter sales of $265.5 million, compared with $252.1 million in the year-ago period. Quarterly net income was $43.2 million, versus $28.5 million.
Other expenses fell to $5 million from $14.7 million a year ago due to lower interest costs, less goodwill due to amortization and higher royalty income, Dollens said.
Gross margin jumped to 75 percent on the first quarter from 69.4 percent a year earlier, largely due to lower costs.
The effective income tax rate on the quarter was 36.5 percent, down from 37.7 percent in the fourth quarter.
"We're comfortable with that lower tax rate going forward...for at least 1997," Dollens said.
In February, Guidant halted European shipments of its Ventak AV implantable defibrillator due to technical problems.
"We have started reshipping and have started implanting," Dollens said, adding that the scope and cost of the problem ended up being smaller than expected.

"That's also one of the reasons we had a lower cost of sale and higher gross margin than we had expected in the first quarter. We had considerably less rework than we thought we were going to have," Dollens said.
